Hi Carlos. Let us start with the numbers. How many producers are in the group now?
There are twelve producers, Emma. And there are two new properties in the region.
Good. And what are you doing right now?
I am preparing the files for the next audit. Ana is updating the records in the system.
Perfect. What did you find on the last visit?
There was no record for one processing unit. It is my main concern, but it is not a critical finding. The evidence is in my report.
Thank you for saying it early. Is the corrective action ready?
Yes. I am going to send the corrective action to the producer on Monday. That is my top priority.
Very good. And remember, the certificate is renewed in December, so we have time.
Understood. Our progress is good -- eighty percent of the actions are closed.

This is how I prepare for a status meeting. First I check the numbers. How many producers are in the group? How many farms are audited this year? Then I write two lines about the work now: what I am doing, and what my team is doing. After that I write what happened on the last visit: what I saw, what I recorded, and where there was a gap. I always say my concern early, and I always bring the evidence. At the end I say the plan: what I am going to do, and when.

Hi Carlos, this is Emma. I read your status note, and I have some feedback for you. First, the good news: your numbers are clear and your note arrived on time. Thank you. Second, one small point for Friday. Do not start with the problem. Start with the progress, then the concern, then the plan. It is easier for the group. And one more thing. When you talk about a gap, always say the corrective action in the same sentence. That is what the auditors do. See you on Friday, Carlos. Good work.
